intro: You can already link ideas with **However**, **Moreover** and **Nevertheless**, and build a paragraph around a topic sentence. Now you'll put paragraphs together into a full essay: an introduction with your position, body paragraphs with arguments and counter-arguments, and a conclusion. You'll also learn exactly what the Cambridge **B2 First** and **IELTS Writing Task 2** essays ask for, and how long to write.
teachingNotes: Builds on b2-linking-words (despite / whereas / nevertheless / consequently / moreover; a paragraph = topic sentence → support → a turn → concluding sentence; a paragraph never opens with Moreover, As a result or For example), b1-writing-stories-articles (one main idea per paragraph, the topic sentence = kalimat utama, paragraf deduktif) and b1-giving-opinions (I think / In my opinion / I believe; *'According to me'). Recap each in a line, don't re-teach them. Two kinds of essay: an OPINION essay (one side from start to end; the other side is mentioned only to answer it) and a DISCURSIVE essay (for and against / discussion: both sides fairly, the writer's own opinion usually in the conclusion, or wherever the question asks for it). Explain jargon the first time: essay (karangan argumentatif), thesis (pernyataan sikap: your position in one sentence), paraphrase (parafrase: same meaning, new words), body paragraph (paragraf isi), counter-argument (kontra-argumen: the other side), refute (membantah).

Structure. Introduction = paraphrase the question (change the words and the sentence shape; don't copy it) + the thesis (In my view, … / I believe that …; in a discursive essay it can say what the essay will do: This essay will look at both sides). Two or three sentences, about 30–50 words. Body paragraphs (2–3 in B2 First, 2–3 in IELTS): one main idea each: topic sentence → explanation (why / how) → example (a fact, a number, a real case: For example, …). Conclusion = In conclusion, / To sum up, + the position again in new words + the main reasons in short. No new ideas, no new examples. Indonesian school-essay habits to name: very long introductions with history, background or dictionary definitions ('Di era globalisasi ini …'); *'As we all know, …' from 'Seperti yang kita ketahui bersama' (filler, and the reader may not know: just state the fact); ending with an appeal ('Let's protect our environment together!' from 'Marilah kita …'). 'Nowadays, …' openings that say nothing ('Nowadays, technology is developing very fast'): mention as a style note only, never test it or mark Nowadays as wrong: it is correct English.

Arguments and counter-arguments. An argument = a reason + support. Showing the other side and answering it makes an essay stronger and more balanced. Patterns: Some people argue / believe / claim that … However, … ; While it is true that …, … (here while = although: a concession, not the 'sedangkan' comparison from b2-linking-words: point this out); Admittedly, …, but … / Admittedly, … . However, …; It could be argued that … Nevertheless, … (a phrase to remember). Refute the IDEA politely, never the people: However, this is not always the case. / This may be true for some people, but … Not: They are wrong. / This idea is stupid. Moreover after the other side's argument is a logic error (it adds, it doesn't answer). Hedging as a tendency: many / most / often / tend to rather than all / always / never. The node's common error: *'In my opinion, I think that …' says the same thing twice: choose one (In my opinion, … / I think … / I believe that … / In my view, …). Also *'According to me' (b1-giving-opinions).

Exam facts, stated exactly (don't invent band scores or exact penalties). Cambridge B2 First Writing: 1 hour 20 minutes, two parts (about 40 minutes each). Part 1 is compulsory: an essay question with two notes; write about BOTH notes and add ONE idea of your own; 140–190 words; give your opinion with reasons. Part 2 is a choice (article, email or letter, review, report), also 140–190 words: name it, don't teach it here. IELTS Writing Task 2 (the same kind of task in Academic and General Training): an essay of AT LEAST 250 words; spend about 40 minutes on it (the whole Writing test is 60 minutes); it counts twice as much as Task 1. Common question types (teachers' labels, not official names): opinion ('To what extent do you agree or disagree?'), discussion ('Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.' Both views AND your opinion), problem-solution ('What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?'); also advantages-disadvantages and two-part questions. Under 250 words loses marks; there's no maximum, but about 260–300 words is a sensible target. Counting tip: on paper, count the words in three typical lines and multiply; IELTS on computer shows a word count.

Style and limits. Exam essays are formal: no contractions (it is, do not), no slang, no exclamation marks, no 'you know'. 'I' is fine when the question asks for your opinion. British spelling (neighbour, organise) and American (neighbor, organize) are both accepted; just be consistent. Grammar: A0–B1 plus b2-linking-words. No participle clauses, non-defining relative clauses (…, which …), third conditional, wish or inversion. When the learner writes a full essay, check the shape first (an introduction with a thesis, body paragraphs with topic sentences, a conclusion with no new ideas, the word count, both notes + an own idea for B2 First, both views + an opinion for an IELTS discussion), then correct one or two language points only, usually the opinion phrase, a linker with the wrong logic, or a copied question.

keyPoints.title: Introduction, body paragraphs, conclusion
keyPoints.explanation: Introduction: the question in your own words + your thesis (your position in one sentence), in two or three sentences. Body paragraphs: one main idea each: topic sentence → explanation → example. Conclusion: your position again in new words and the main reasons in short, with no new ideas. An opinion essay argues for one side; a discursive essay shows both sides fairly and gives the opinion at the end.

examples.en: In my view, this trend brings real benefits, but online shopping should not replace markets completely.
examples.id: Menurut saya, tren ini membawa manfaat nyata, tetapi belanja online sebaiknya tidak menggantikan pasar sepenuhnya.

examples.en: The main advantage of online shopping is convenience.
examples.id: Keuntungan utama belanja online adalah kepraktisannya.

examples.en: In conclusion, I believe that online shopping is a useful addition to our lives.
examples.id: Kesimpulannya, saya yakin belanja online adalah tambahan yang berguna dalam hidup kita.

id.title: Pembuka, paragraf isi, penutup
id.explanation: Pembuka (introduction): pertanyaannya dengan kata-katamu sendiri + thesis (posisimu dalam satu kalimat), dalam dua atau tiga kalimat. Paragraf isi: satu ide pokok per paragraf: topic sentence → penjelasan → contoh. Penutup (conclusion): posisimu lagi dengan kata-kata baru dan alasan utamanya secara singkat, tanpa ide baru. Esai opini membela satu sisi; esai diskursif menunjukkan kedua sisi secara adil dan memberi pendapat di akhir.

keyPoints.title: Arguments and counter-arguments, answered politely
keyPoints.explanation: An argument is a reason with support. Show the other side (the counter-argument), then answer it politely: Some people argue that … However, … / While it is true that …, … / Admittedly, …, but …. Answer the idea, not the people. Give your opinion with one phrase: In my opinion, … or I believe that …, not 'In my opinion, I think …'.

examples.en: Some people argue that working from home makes staff lazy. However, many remote workers are actually more productive.
examples.id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa kerja dari rumah membuat staf malas. Namun, banyak pekerja jarak jauh justru lebih produktif.

examples.en: While it is true that cars are convenient, they cause serious traffic jams in Jakarta.
examples.id: Memang benar mobil itu praktis, tetapi mobil menyebabkan kemacetan parah di Jakarta.

examples.en: Admittedly, electric motorbikes are expensive, but they are much cheaper to run.
examples.id: Memang harus diakui motor listrik itu mahal, tetapi biaya pemakaiannya jauh lebih murah.

id.title: Argumen dan kontra-argumen, dijawab dengan sopan
id.explanation: Argumen adalah alasan beserta pendukungnya. Tunjukkan sisi sebaliknya (kontra-argumen), lalu jawab dengan sopan: Some people argue that … However, … / While it is true that …, … / Admittedly, …, but …. Bantah idenya, bukan orangnya. Sampaikan pendapatmu dengan satu ungkapan saja: In my opinion, … atau I believe that …, bukan 'In my opinion, I think …'.

keyPoints.title: B2 First and IELTS Task 2: the task and the length
keyPoints.explanation: Cambridge B2 First, Writing Part 1 (compulsory): an essay question with two notes. Write about both notes and add one idea of your own, in 140–190 words (about 40 minutes). IELTS Writing Task 2: an essay of at least 250 words in about 40 minutes of the 60-minute test; it counts twice as much as Task 1. Read the question type: opinion, discussion (both views + your opinion) or problem-solution.

examples.en: To what extent do you agree or disagree?
examples.id: Sejauh mana kamu setuju atau tidak setuju? (tipe opini)

examples.en: Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
examples.id: Bahas kedua pandangan ini dan berikan pendapatmu sendiri. (tipe diskusi)

examples.en: What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?
examples.id: Masalah apa yang ditimbulkannya, dan apa yang bisa dilakukan untuk mengatasinya? (tipe masalah-solusi)

id.title: B2 First dan IELTS Task 2: tugasnya dan panjangnya
id.explanation: Cambridge B2 First, Writing Part 1 (wajib): pertanyaan esai dengan dua catatan (notes). Tulis tentang kedua catatan itu dan tambahkan satu ide milikmu sendiri, dalam 140–190 kata (sekitar 40 menit). IELTS Writing Task 2: esai minimal 250 kata dalam sekitar 40 menit dari tes 60 menit; bobotnya dua kali Task 1. Baca tipe pertanyaannya: opini, diskusi (kedua pandangan + pendapatmu) atau masalah-solusi.

guidedPractice.prompt: Paraphrase this essay question in one sentence for your introduction (same meaning, your own words): 'Many young Indonesians now prefer to work for start-ups rather than for big companies.'
expected: a growing number of young people in indonesia would rather work for a start-up than for a large company
more and more young indonesians choose start-ups instead of large companies
these days many young people in indonesia want to join a start-up rather than a big firm
guidedPractice.hint: Change the words (young Indonesians → young people in Indonesia, big → large, prefer → would rather / choose) and the shape of the sentence. Don't copy the question.

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the letters in the best order for a body paragraph. A: For example, a teacher in Surabaya now runs her whole course with free online tools. B: Technology has made learning much cheaper for many Indonesians. C: Many courses and apps are free or cost less than one printed book.
guidedPractice.hint: Topic sentence (the main idea) → explanation → example. A sentence that starts with For example can't open a paragraph.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one linker that answers the other side: Some people argue that homework is a waste of time. ___, it helps students remember what they learnt in class.
guidedPractice.hint: A full stop before the gap and a comma after it, and the idea turns to the other side: a contrast linker that starts a new sentence.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite this sentence so it's polite enough for an essay. Keep the idea of the other side and add a short reply: 'People who say that cars should be banned from the city centre are wrong.'
expected: some people argue that cars should be banned from the city centre however this would make life difficult for elderly and disabled people
while it is true that banning cars would reduce pollution it would make it harder for many people to reach the city centre
admittedly a ban on cars would make the air cleaner but many people would have no other way to get to work
guidedPractice.hint: Present the idea neutrally (Some people argue that … / While it is true that … / Admittedly, …), then answer the IDEA with a reason, not the people.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which IELTS Task 2 type is this question? Write opinion, discussion or problem-solution. 'Young people should do a year of community service before they start university. To what extent do you agree or disagree?'
guidedPractice.hint: 'To what extent do you agree or disagree?' asks for YOUR position, argued from start to end.

independentPractice.prompt: B2 First, Writing Part 1. Write an essay of 140–190 words. 'Every young person should learn to drive a car. Do you agree?' Notes: write about 1. jobs 2. safety 3. ___ (your own idea). Checklist: an introduction (paraphrase + thesis); one body paragraph per note, plus your own idea; a topic sentence in each; one counter-argument answered politely; a conclusion with no new ideas; formal style, no contractions.
expected: many people see driving as a basic skill for every young adult in my view learning to drive is useful but it should not be compulsory for everyone the strongest argument for learning to drive is jobs many companies in indonesia ask for a driving licence for example sales staff often visit clients in different parts of the city so they need a car or a motorbike safety is another important point some people argue that young drivers become careful after proper lessons while it is true that lessons help young drivers still tend to have more accidents than older drivers a third point is that public transport in cities like jakarta is improving fast with the mrt and the krl many young people can now get to work without a car at all in conclusion i believe that learning to drive is a good idea for people who need it for work however it should remain a choice rather than a rule
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: both notes covered + one clear idea of your own; 140–190 words; thesis in the introduction; topic sentence → explanation → example in each body paragraph; a counter-argument answered politely (Some people argue … However, … / While it is true that …, …); conclusion restates the position with no new ideas; one opinion phrase, not 'In my opinion, I think'.

independentPractice.prompt: IELTS Writing Task 2 (40 minutes, at least 250 words). 'Some people believe that children should start learning English at primary school, while others think they should first master their own language. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.' Plan first: one body paragraph for each view, then your opinion.
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: at least 250 words; introduction = paraphrase + what the essay will do or your position; body 1 = the first view with reasons and an example; body 2 = the second view with reasons and an example; your own opinion stated clearly (in the introduction and/or conclusion); conclusion with no new ideas; formal style.

independentPractice.prompt: Write an introduction (2–3 sentences, about 30–50 words) for this IELTS question: 'Social media does more harm than good to teenagers. To what extent do you agree or disagree?' Paraphrase the question, then give your thesis.
expected: today most teenagers spend several hours a day on platforms such as instagram and tiktok some people believe that this does them more harm than good i largely agree because social media can damage young people's sleep and self-confidence
independentPractice.hint: Sentence 1: the question in your own words (no 'As we all know', no long background). Sentence 2–3: your position, with one opinion phrase (I believe … / In my view …), and maybe the two main reasons.

assessment.prompt: Essay question: 'Mobile phones should be banned in secondary schools. Do you agree?' Which sentence is the best thesis (the writer's position) for the introduction? Write A, B or C. A: Mobile phones are very popular among teenagers in Indonesia. B: In this essay, I will write about mobile phones in schools. C: I believe that schools should ban phones during lessons, as they distract students from learning.
assessment.rubric: Correct: C (it gives a clear position on the question, with a reason). A = 0 (a general fact with no position). B = 0 (it announces the topic but doesn't say what the writer thinks).

assessment.prompt: Read the conclusion of an essay about transport in Jakarta. One sentence should be removed, because it adds a new idea. Write its number. '(1) In conclusion, I believe that the government should spend more money on public transport than on new roads. (2) Better trains and buses reduce both traffic jams and air pollution. (3) The government should also build more hospitals in small towns. (4) For these reasons, money spent on the MRT and the KRL is money well spent.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: 3 (hospitals are a new idea that has nothing to do with transport; a conclusion only restates the position and the main reasons). 1 = 0 (it restates the position). 2 = 0 (it sums up the main reasons). 4 = 0 (it closes the essay).

assessment.prompt: Write one word to complete the sentence. It shows the other side and then answers it: '___ it is true that online classes are cheaper, they cannot replace face-to-face contact with a teacher.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: While (here while = although: the writer accepts one point, then answers it). Although / Though / Whilst = 100. 'Even though' = 80 (right meaning, but two words and unusual before 'it is true that'). 'Whereas' = 20 (it compares two facts, it doesn't accept a point). 'However', 'Despite' or 'Moreover' = 0 (However starts a new sentence, despite needs a noun, Moreover adds).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in this thesis sentence: In my opinion, I think that public transport in Jakarta should be free.
acceptableAnswers: in my opinion public transport in jakarta should be free
i think that public transport in jakarta should be free
i think public transport in jakarta should be free
i believe that public transport in jakarta should be free
i believe public transport in jakarta should be free
in my view public transport in jakarta should be free
i strongly believe that public transport in jakarta should be free
i strongly believe public transport in jakarta should be free
i feel that public transport in jakarta should be free
personally i think that public transport in jakarta should be free
personally i think public transport in jakarta should be free
i would argue that public transport in jakarta should be free
assessment.rubric: Correct: one opinion phrase only: In my opinion, … / I think (that) … / I believe (that) … / In my view, …. 'According to me, …' = 30 (one phrase, but not natural English). The sentence unchanged = 0 (In my opinion and I think say the same thing twice). A changed meaning (e.g. 'should not be free') = 0.

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani is preparing her class for the Cambridge B2 First exam. How long must the Writing Part 1 essay be? Write the minimum and the maximum number of words.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 140–190 words. Only one number right (e.g. 140–200, 120–190) = 40. 250 = 0 (that's the IELTS Task 2 minimum). 100 or 120–180 = 0.

assessment.prompt: Dimas is taking IELTS in Surabaya next month. What is the minimum number of words for his Writing Task 2 essay? Write the number.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 250 (at least 250 words; there's no maximum). 150 = 20 (that's Task 1). 140, 190 or 140–190 = 0 (that's B2 First). 300 = 30 (a sensible target, but not the minimum).

assessment.prompt: In the B2 First essay, Sari gets this task: 'Is it better to live in a big city or a small town? Notes: write about 1. jobs 2. the cost of living 3. ___ (your own idea).' She must write about both notes. How many ideas of her own must she add? Write the number.
assessment.rubric: Correct: one (both notes + one different idea of her own). 'two' or 'three' = 0 (the two notes are given; she adds one). 'none' or 'zero' = 0 (the third idea is compulsory).

material.title: Two kinds of essay, one clear shape

blocks.text:
Quick recap: a paragraph has **one main idea**, given in its **topic sentence**, and linkers like *Moreover, Nevertheless* and *As a result* show how the sentences connect. An **essay** puts several of those paragraphs together to answer **one question**.

There are two kinds:
- **Opinion essay**: you choose **one side** and argue for it from start to end. You can mention the other side, but only to answer it.
- **Discursive essay** (also called a *for and against* or *discussion* essay; *diskursif* = membahas): you show **both sides fairly**, and give your own opinion at the end (or wherever the question asks for it).

Both kinds have the same shape:
1. **Introduction**: the question in your own words + your **thesis** (*pernyataan sikap*: your position in one sentence).
2. **Body paragraphs** (*paragraf isi*), usually two or three: one main idea each.
3. **Conclusion**: your position again, in new words. **No new ideas.**

Here's a B2 First task and an essay of 174 words. The task: *In many Indonesian cities, people now buy food and household goods online instead of at traditional markets. Is this a good development?* Notes: write about **1. convenience**, **2. prices**, **3. your own idea**.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: sebuah paragraf punya **satu ide pokok**, yang ada di **topic sentence**-nya (kalimat utama), dan kata penghubung seperti *Moreover, Nevertheless* dan *As a result* menunjukkan hubungan antarkalimat. **Esai** (*essay*, karangan argumentatif) menggabungkan beberapa paragraf seperti itu untuk menjawab **satu pertanyaan**.

Ada dua jenis:
- **Esai opini** (*opinion essay*): kamu memilih **satu sisi** dan membelanya dari awal sampai akhir. Kamu boleh menyebut sisi sebaliknya, tapi hanya untuk menjawabnya.
- **Esai diskursif** (*discursive essay*, disebut juga *for and against* atau *discussion essay*; diskursif = membahas): kamu menunjukkan **kedua sisi secara adil**, lalu memberi pendapatmu sendiri di akhir (atau di bagian yang diminta pertanyaannya).

Keduanya punya bentuk yang sama:
1. **Introduction** (pembuka): pertanyaannya dengan kata-katamu sendiri + **thesis** (*pernyataan sikap*: posisimu dalam satu kalimat).
2. **Body paragraphs** (*paragraf isi*), biasanya dua atau tiga: satu ide pokok per paragraf.
3. **Conclusion** (penutup): posisimu lagi, dengan kata-kata baru. **Tanpa ide baru.**

Ini contoh tugas B2 First dan esai sepanjang 174 kata. Tugasnya: *In many Indonesian cities, people now buy food and household goods online instead of at traditional markets. Is this a good development?* Catatan (notes): tulis tentang **1. convenience** (kepraktisan), **2. prices** (harga), **3. idemu sendiri**.

rows.en: More and more people in Indonesian cities now order their shopping through apps instead of going to a traditional market. In my view, this trend brings real benefits, but online shopping should not replace markets completely.
rows.id: Semakin banyak orang di kota-kota Indonesia kini memesan belanjaan lewat aplikasi alih-alih pergi ke pasar tradisional. Menurut saya, tren ini membawa manfaat nyata, tetapi belanja online sebaiknya tidak menggantikan pasar sepenuhnya.
rows.note: introduction: the question in new words + the thesis

id.note: pembuka: pertanyaannya dengan kata-kata baru + thesis

rows.en: The main advantage of online shopping is convenience. Busy office workers can order groceries on the KRL home and receive them the same evening. For example, my neighbour in Bekasi saves about three hours every weekend because she no longer drives to the market.
rows.id: Keuntungan utama belanja online adalah kepraktisannya. Pekerja kantor yang sibuk bisa memesan belanjaan di KRL saat pulang dan menerimanya malam itu juga. Contohnya, tetangga saya di Bekasi menghemat sekitar tiga jam setiap akhir pekan karena dia tidak lagi menyetir ke pasar.

rows.en: Some people argue that prices are lower online. While it is true that apps often offer discounts, market traders usually sell fresh vegetables more cheaply, and buyers can bargain.
rows.id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa harga online lebih murah. Memang benar aplikasi sering memberi diskon, tetapi pedagang pasar biasanya menjual sayur segar lebih murah, dan pembeli bisa menawar.
rows.note: body 2 (note 2): the other side, then a polite answer

id.note: isi 2 (catatan 2): sisi sebaliknya, lalu jawaban yang sopan

rows.en: Another reason to keep markets is that they matter to local communities. Thousands of small traders depend on them for a living, and shoppers can talk to the sellers and choose exactly what they want.
rows.id: Alasan lain untuk mempertahankan pasar adalah pasar penting bagi masyarakat setempat. Ribuan pedagang kecil menggantungkan hidup darinya, dan pembeli bisa mengobrol dengan penjual dan memilih persis yang mereka mau.

rows.en: In conclusion, I believe that online shopping is a useful addition to our lives. Nevertheless, we should keep supporting traditional markets, as they offer good prices and keep communities together.
rows.id: Kesimpulannya, saya yakin belanja online adalah tambahan yang berguna dalam hidup kita. Namun demikian, kita sebaiknya tetap mendukung pasar tradisional, karena pasar menawarkan harga yang baik dan menjaga kebersamaan masyarakat.
rows.note: conclusion: the position again + the main reasons, no new idea

id.note: penutup: posisinya lagi + alasan utamanya, tanpa ide baru

blocks.text:
Look at how the paragraphs start: *The main advantage …*, *Some people argue …*, *Another reason …*. Each one opens with its **topic sentence**, never with *Moreover* or *For example* (they point back to something before). *In conclusion* is the exception: it opens the **last** paragraph.

*neighbour* is British spelling; Americans write *neighbor*. Both are fine in the exams: just don't mix them in one essay.

id.text:
Perhatikan cara paragraf-paragrafnya dimulai: *The main advantage …*, *Some people argue …*, *Another reason …*. Setiap paragraf dibuka dengan **topic sentence**-nya, tidak pernah dengan *Moreover* atau *For example* (kata-kata itu merujuk ke sesuatu sebelumnya). *In conclusion* pengecualiannya: kata ini membuka paragraf **terakhir**.

*neighbour* ejaan Inggris Britania; orang Amerika menulis *neighbor*. Keduanya boleh dalam ujian: asal jangan dicampur dalam satu esai.

blocks.prompt: In the model essay, which paragraph gives the writer's own idea (note 3)?
blocks.explain: The task gave two notes, **convenience** and **prices**: the second and third paragraphs cover them. The **fourth** paragraph adds the writer's own idea: markets matter to **local communities**. In B2 First you always write about both notes and add one idea of your own.

id.prompt: Dalam contoh esainya, paragraf mana yang berisi ide penulis sendiri (catatan 3)?
id.explain: Tugasnya memberi dua catatan, **convenience** dan **prices**: paragraf kedua dan ketiga membahasnya. Paragraf **keempat** menambahkan ide penulis sendiri: pasar penting bagi **masyarakat setempat** (*local communities*). Di B2 First kamu selalu menulis tentang kedua catatan dan menambahkan satu ide milikmu sendiri.

id.title: Dua jenis esai, satu bentuk yang jelas

material.title: The introduction, the body and the conclusion

blocks.text:
**The introduction: short and to the point.** Two or three sentences (about 30–50 words):
1. **Paraphrase** the question (*parafrase*: the same meaning in new words). Change the words **and** the shape of the sentence. Don't copy the question: copied words don't show your English.
2. Give your **thesis**: your position in one clear sentence. *In my view, … / I believe that … / I strongly believe that …* In a discursive essay you can also say what the essay will do: *This essay will look at both sides.*

**Body paragraphs: one main idea each.**
1. **Topic sentence**: the point of the paragraph.
2. **Explanation**: why or how it's true.
3. **Example**: a fact, a number or a real case: *For example, …*

**The conclusion: no surprises.** Start with *In conclusion,* or *To sum up,*. Give your position again in **new words** and the main reasons in short. **No new ideas and no new examples.** In a discursive essay, *On balance, …* (*setelah menimbang semuanya*) is a good way to give your final opinion.

id.text:
**Pembuka: singkat dan langsung.** Dua atau tiga kalimat (sekitar 30–50 kata):
1. **Parafrasekan** pertanyaannya (*paraphrase*: makna yang sama dengan kata-kata baru). Ubah kata-katanya **dan** bentuk kalimatnya. Jangan menyalin pertanyaannya: kata-kata yang disalin tidak menunjukkan kemampuan bahasa Inggrismu.
2. Berikan **thesis**-mu: posisimu dalam satu kalimat yang jelas. *In my view, … / I believe that … / I strongly believe that …* Di esai diskursif kamu juga bisa menyebut apa yang akan dibahas esainya: *This essay will look at both sides.*

**Paragraf isi: satu ide pokok per paragraf.**
1. **Topic sentence**: inti paragrafnya.
2. **Penjelasan** (*explanation*): kenapa atau bagaimana itu benar.
3. **Contoh** (*example*): fakta, angka atau kasus nyata: *For example, …*

**Penutup: tanpa kejutan.** Mulai dengan *In conclusion,* atau *To sum up,*. Sampaikan posisimu lagi dengan **kata-kata baru** dan alasan utamanya secara singkat. **Tanpa ide baru dan tanpa contoh baru.** Di esai diskursif, *On balance, …* (setelah menimbang semuanya) cara yang bagus untuk memberi pendapat akhirmu.

rows.en: Many companies now let their staff work from home.
rows.id: Banyak perusahaan sekarang mengizinkan stafnya bekerja dari rumah.

rows.en: Working from home has become a normal part of office life for a growing number of employees.
rows.id: Bekerja dari rumah sudah menjadi bagian biasa dari kehidupan kantor bagi semakin banyak karyawan.
rows.note: a paraphrase: new words, new shape

rows.en: I strongly believe that this change is good for both workers and companies.
rows.id: Saya sangat yakin perubahan ini baik bagi pekerja maupun perusahaan.

rows.en: To sum up, working from home saves time and money, so companies should offer it whenever possible.
rows.id: Singkatnya, bekerja dari rumah menghemat waktu dan uang, jadi perusahaan sebaiknya menawarkannya bila memungkinkan.
rows.note: a conclusion: the position again + the main reasons

rows.en: On balance, I believe that the advantages are greater than the disadvantages.
rows.id: Setelah menimbang semuanya, saya yakin kelebihannya lebih besar daripada kekurangannya.
rows.note: the final opinion in a discursive essay

blocks.text:
**School-essay habits to leave behind:**
- **A long introduction** with history, background or dictionary definitions (*Di era globalisasi ini …*). In English exams, get to your position in two or three sentences.
- `As we all know, …` (from *Seperti yang kita ketahui bersama*): it fills space, and the reader may not know. Just say the fact.
- **An appeal at the end** (*Marilah kita …* → `Let's protect our environment together!`). An English essay ends with your position and reasons, not a call to action.
- **A style note**: many essays start with *Nowadays, technology is developing very fast.* *Nowadays* is correct English, but a sentence like this could open any essay and says nothing. Start with the topic of the question instead.

id.text:
**Kebiasaan esai sekolah yang perlu ditinggalkan:**
- **Pembuka yang panjang** berisi sejarah, latar belakang atau definisi kamus (*Di era globalisasi ini …*). Dalam ujian bahasa Inggris, sampaikan posisimu dalam dua atau tiga kalimat.
- `As we all know, …` (dari *Seperti yang kita ketahui bersama*): hanya mengisi tempat, dan pembaca belum tentu tahu. Sampaikan saja faktanya.
- **Ajakan di akhir** (*Marilah kita …* → `Let's protect our environment together!`). Esai bahasa Inggris diakhiri dengan posisimu dan alasannya, bukan ajakan.
- **Catatan gaya**: banyak esai dimulai dengan *Nowadays, technology is developing very fast.* *Nowadays* itu bahasa Inggris yang benar, tapi kalimat seperti ini bisa membuka esai apa saja dan tidak mengatakan apa-apa. Lebih baik mulai langsung dengan topik pertanyaannya.

blocks.prompt: These three sentences make one body paragraph. Which one is the topic sentence?
options: For example, many ojek online drivers choose their own working hours.
Gig work gives many Indonesians flexible jobs.
This means they can study or look after their children at the same time.
blocks.explain: The topic sentence gives the main idea of the paragraph: **gig work gives flexible jobs** (*gig work* = kerja lepas lewat aplikasi). The sentence with *This means* explains it, and *For example* gives a real case: both point back, so they can't open the paragraph.

id.prompt: Ketiga kalimat ini membentuk satu paragraf isi. Mana topic sentence-nya?
id.explain: Topic sentence memberi ide pokok paragrafnya: **gig work memberi pekerjaan yang fleksibel** (*gig work* = kerja lepas lewat aplikasi). Kalimat dengan *This means* menjelaskannya, dan *For example* memberi kasus nyata: keduanya merujuk ke belakang, jadi tidak bisa membuka paragraf.

blocks.text:
An **argument** is a reason for your position, with support (an explanation and an example). A **counter-argument** (*kontra-argumen*) is the other side. Showing it and answering it makes your essay stronger: the reader sees that you have thought about both sides.

First **show** the other side, then **refute** it (*membantah*) politely:
- *Some people argue / believe / claim that … **However,** …*
- ***While it is true that** …, …* (careful: here **while = although**: you accept one point, then answer it. It's not the *sedangkan* comparison from the linking-words lesson.)
- ***Admittedly,** …, **but** …* (*memang harus diakui …, tetapi …*)
- ***It could be argued that** … **Nevertheless,** …* (a phrase to remember)

Answer the **idea**, not the people: *However, this is not always the case.* / *This may be true for some people, but …* Never *They are wrong* or *This idea is stupid*.

**Where does it go?** In an **opinion essay**, the counter-argument usually gets one body paragraph (or part of one), and you answer it there. In a **discursive essay**, each side gets its own paragraph, and your opinion comes at the end.

id.text:
**Argumen** adalah alasan untuk posisimu, beserta pendukungnya (penjelasan dan contoh). **Kontra-argumen** (*counter-argument*) adalah sisi sebaliknya. Menunjukkan dan menjawabnya membuat esaimu lebih kuat: pembaca melihat bahwa kamu sudah memikirkan kedua sisi.

Pertama **tunjukkan** sisi sebaliknya, lalu **bantah** (*refute*) dengan sopan:
- *Some people argue / believe / claim that … **However,** …*
- ***While it is true that** …, …* (hati-hati: di sini **while = although**: kamu menerima satu poin, lalu menjawabnya. Ini bukan *while* = *sedangkan* untuk membandingkan dari pelajaran kata penghubung.)
- ***Admittedly,** …, **but** …* (memang harus diakui …, tetapi …)
- ***It could be argued that** … **Nevertheless,** …* (ungkapan untuk diingat saja)

Jawab **idenya**, bukan orangnya: *However, this is not always the case.* / *This may be true for some people, but …* Jangan *They are wrong* atau *This idea is stupid*.

**Letaknya di mana?** Di **esai opini**, kontra-argumen biasanya mendapat satu paragraf isi (atau sebagian), dan kamu menjawabnya di situ. Di **esai diskursif**, setiap sisi mendapat paragrafnya sendiri, dan pendapatmu ada di akhir.

rows.en: Some people argue that working from home makes staff lazy. However, many remote workers are actually more productive.
rows.id: Sebagian orang berpendapat bahwa kerja dari rumah membuat staf malas. Namun, banyak pekerja jarak jauh justru lebih produktif.

rows.en: While it is true that cars are convenient, they cause serious traffic jams in Jakarta.
rows.id: Memang benar mobil itu praktis, tetapi mobil menyebabkan kemacetan parah di Jakarta.

rows.en: Admittedly, electric motorbikes are expensive, but they are much cheaper to run.
rows.id: Memang harus diakui motor listrik itu mahal, tetapi biaya pemakaiannya jauh lebih murah.

rows.en: It could be argued that exams cause too much stress. Nevertheless, they show clearly what students have learnt.
rows.id: Bisa saja dikatakan bahwa ujian menimbulkan terlalu banyak stres. Namun demikian, ujian menunjukkan dengan jelas apa yang sudah dipelajari siswa.
rows.note: It could be argued that … (a phrase to remember)

id.note: It could be argued that … (ungkapan untuk diingat)

rows.en: This may be true for some families, but most parents in big cities need two incomes.
rows.id: Ini mungkin benar untuk sebagian keluarga, tetapi kebanyakan orang tua di kota besar butuh dua penghasilan.
rows.note: a polite answer: some … but most …

id.note: jawaban yang sopan: some … but most …

blocks.text:
**Give your opinion once.** `In my opinion, I think that …` ✗: *In my opinion* and *I think* mean the same thing, so you say it twice. Choose one: *In my opinion, … / I think … / I believe that … / In my view, …*. And remember `According to me` ✗ (from *menurut saya*).

**Careful with big words.** *all, always, never, everyone* are easy to attack. Essays usually sound more convincing with *many, most, often, usually* or *tend to*: *Young drivers **tend to** take more risks.*

id.text:
**Sampaikan pendapatmu sekali saja.** `In my opinion, I think that …` ✗: *In my opinion* dan *I think* artinya sama, jadi kamu mengatakannya dua kali. Pilih satu: *In my opinion, … / I think … / I believe that … / In my view, …*. Dan ingat `According to me` ✗ (dari *menurut saya*).

**Hati-hati dengan kata yang terlalu mutlak.** *all, always, never, everyone* mudah dibantah. Esai biasanya terdengar lebih meyakinkan dengan *many, most, often, usually* atau *tend to* (cenderung): *Young drivers **tend to** take more risks.*

blocks.prompt: Which word fits the gap? Admittedly, the MRT is expensive for some workers, ___ it is much faster than driving.
blocks.explain: *Admittedly, …, but …*: the writer accepts a point (it's expensive), then answers it (it's faster). **but** joins the two parts inside one sentence. *moreover* adds a point on the same side and starts a new sentence, and *despite* needs a noun or -ing after it.

id.prompt: Kata mana yang cocok? Admittedly, the MRT is expensive for some workers, ___ it is much faster than driving.
id.explain: *Admittedly, …, but …*: penulis menerima satu poin (mahal), lalu menjawabnya (lebih cepat). **but** menyambungkan dua bagian di dalam satu kalimat. *moreover* menambah poin di sisi yang sama dan memulai kalimat baru, dan *despite* butuh kata benda atau -ing setelahnya.

material.title: Exam essays: B2 First and IELTS Task 2

blocks.text:
**Cambridge B2 First, Writing.** The paper is 1 hour 20 minutes, with two parts (so about 40 minutes each).
- **Part 1 is compulsory** (*wajib*): an essay. You get a question and **two notes**. Write about **both notes** and add **one idea of your own**.
- **Length: 140–190 words.** Under 140, you usually haven't covered everything; over 190, you waste time and make more mistakes.
- Part 2 is a choice (an article, an email or letter, a review or a report), also 140–190 words.

**IELTS Writing Task 2** (the same kind of task in IELTS Academic and General Training).
- An essay of **at least 250 words**. Shorter answers lose marks. There's no maximum, but about 260–300 words is a sensible target.
- Spend about **40 minutes** on it: the whole Writing test is 60 minutes, and Task 2 counts **twice as much** as Task 1.
- Read the question type (teachers' names for them, not official ones):
  - **opinion**: *To what extent do you agree or disagree?* → one clear position, from start to end;
  - **discussion**: *Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.* → a paragraph for each view **and** your opinion;
  - **problem-solution**: *What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?* → a paragraph for the problems, one for the solutions.
  You may also meet advantages-disadvantages questions and two-part questions: answer **every** part.

A 40-minute plan: about 5 minutes to plan, 30 to write, 5 to check.

id.text:
**Cambridge B2 First, Writing.** Tesnya 1 jam 20 menit, dengan dua bagian (jadi sekitar 40 menit per bagian).
- **Part 1 wajib** (*compulsory*): sebuah esai. Kamu mendapat pertanyaan dan **dua catatan** (notes). Tulis tentang **kedua catatan** dan tambahkan **satu ide milikmu sendiri**.
- **Panjang: 140–190 kata.** Di bawah 140, biasanya belum semuanya terbahas; di atas 190, kamu membuang waktu dan membuat lebih banyak kesalahan.
- Part 2 pilihan (artikel, email atau surat, review atau laporan), juga 140–190 kata.

**IELTS Writing Task 2** (jenis tugas yang sama di IELTS Academic dan General Training).
- Esai **minimal 250 kata**. Jawaban yang lebih pendek kehilangan nilai. Tidak ada batas maksimal, tapi sekitar 260–300 kata target yang masuk akal.
- Pakai sekitar **40 menit** untuk tugas ini: seluruh tes Writing 60 menit, dan bobot Task 2 **dua kali** Task 1.
- Baca tipe pertanyaannya (nama dari para guru, bukan nama resmi):
  - **opini** (*opinion*): *To what extent do you agree or disagree?* → satu posisi yang jelas, dari awal sampai akhir;
  - **diskusi** (*discussion*): *Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.* → satu paragraf untuk setiap pandangan **dan** pendapatmu;
  - **masalah-solusi** (*problem-solution*): *What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?* → satu paragraf untuk masalahnya, satu untuk solusinya.
  Kamu juga bisa bertemu pertanyaan kelebihan-kekurangan dan pertanyaan dua bagian: jawab **setiap** bagiannya.

Rencana 40 menit: sekitar 5 menit merencanakan, 30 menit menulis, 5 menit memeriksa.

rows.en: Some people think that young people should be free to choose any university subject. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
rows.id: Sebagian orang berpikir bahwa anak muda sebaiknya bebas memilih jurusan kuliah apa pun. Sejauh mana kamu setuju atau tidak setuju?

rows.en: Some people believe that tourism helps local communities, while others think it damages them. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
rows.id: Sebagian orang yakin pariwisata membantu masyarakat setempat, sementara yang lain berpikir pariwisata merusaknya. Bahas kedua pandangan ini dan berikan pendapatmu sendiri.
rows.note: IELTS discussion question: both views + your opinion

id.note: pertanyaan IELTS tipe diskusi: kedua pandangan + pendapatmu

rows.en: Many big cities have serious problems with plastic waste. What problems does this cause, and what can be done to solve them?
rows.id: Banyak kota besar punya masalah serius dengan sampah plastik. Masalah apa yang ditimbulkannya, dan apa yang bisa dilakukan untuk mengatasinya?

blocks.text:
**Counting words on paper:** don't count every word. Count the words in three normal lines, take the average, and multiply by the number of lines. (IELTS on computer shows the word count for you.)

**Exam essays are formal:** no contractions (*it is*, not *it's*; *do not*, not *don't*), no slang, no exclamation marks. *I* is fine when the question asks for your opinion.

**Before you finish, check:** a paraphrase and a clear thesis · one main idea per body paragraph, each with a topic sentence · the other side answered politely · a conclusion with no new ideas · B2 First: both notes + your own idea, 140–190 words · IELTS: every part of the question, at least 250 words.

id.text:
**Menghitung kata di kertas:** jangan hitung satu per satu. Hitung kata di tiga baris biasa, ambil rata-ratanya, lalu kalikan dengan jumlah barisnya. (IELTS di komputer menampilkan jumlah katanya.)

**Esai ujian itu formal:** tanpa singkatan (*it is*, bukan *it's*; *do not*, bukan *don't*), tanpa bahasa gaul, tanpa tanda seru. *I* boleh dipakai kalau pertanyaannya meminta pendapatmu.

**Sebelum selesai, periksa:** parafrase dan thesis yang jelas · satu ide pokok per paragraf isi, masing-masing dengan topic sentence · sisi sebaliknya dijawab dengan sopan · penutup tanpa ide baru · B2 First: kedua catatan + idemu sendiri, 140–190 kata · IELTS: setiap bagian pertanyaan, minimal 250 kata.

blocks.prompt: An IELTS question ends: 'What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?' Which type is it?
blocks.explain: It asks for **causes** and **measures** (*langkah-langkah*) to solve the problem: a **problem-solution** question. Plan one paragraph for the causes and one for the solutions. An opinion question asks how far you agree; a discussion question asks you to discuss two views.

id.prompt: Sebuah pertanyaan IELTS diakhiri dengan: 'What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?' Tipe apa ini?
id.explain: Pertanyaannya meminta **penyebab** (*causes*) dan **langkah-langkah** (*measures*) untuk mengatasi masalahnya: tipe **masalah-solusi** (*problem-solution*). Rencanakan satu paragraf untuk penyebabnya dan satu untuk solusinya. Pertanyaan opini menanyakan seberapa jauh kamu setuju; pertanyaan diskusi memintamu membahas dua pandangan.

resources.title: An opinion essay

It's close to IELTS length.

Panjangnya mendekati esai IELTS.

resources.title: B2 First: exam format
resources.note: The official page for the whole B2 First exam. In the Writing section: 1 hour 20 minutes, a compulsory Part 1 essay with two given ideas plus one of your own, and 140–190 words for each part. It also describes the Reading, Listening and Speaking papers.

resources.title: IELTS Academic format: Writing
resources.note: The official description of IELTS Academic Writing: Task 2 is an essay of at least 250 words, you should spend about 40 minutes on it, and it counts twice as much as Task 1. Task 1 (describing a chart or diagram) is a different task. In General Training, Task 1 is a letter, but Task 2 is the same kind of essay.

id.note: Penjelasan resmi IELTS Academic Writing: Task 2 adalah esai minimal 250 kata, sebaiknya dikerjakan sekitar 40 menit, dan bobotnya dua kali Task 1. Task 1 (mendeskripsikan grafik atau diagram) tugas yang berbeda. Di General Training, Task 1 berupa surat, tetapi Task 2 jenis esai yang sama.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa menghubungkan ide dengan **However**, **Moreover** dan **Nevertheless**, dan menyusun paragraf di sekitar topic sentence. Sekarang kamu akan menggabungkan paragraf-paragraf menjadi esai utuh: pembuka dengan posisimu, paragraf isi dengan argumen dan kontra-argumen, dan penutup. Kamu juga akan belajar persis apa yang diminta esai Cambridge **B2 First** dan **IELTS Writing Task 2**, dan berapa panjang yang harus kamu tulis.
suggestedQuestions: Apa bedanya esai opini dan esai diskursif?
Bagaimana cara memparafrasekan pertanyaan tanpa menyalinnya?
Di mana sebaiknya kontra-argumen diletakkan dalam esaiku?

assessment.ess-1: Pertanyaan esai: 'Mobile phones should be banned in secondary schools. Do you agree?' Kalimat mana yang menjadi thesis terbaik (posisi penulis) untuk pembukanya? Tulis A, B atau C. A: Mobile phones are very popular among teenagers in Indonesia. B: In this essay, I will write about mobile phones in schools. C: I believe that schools should ban phones during lessons, as they distract students from learning.
assessment.ess-2: Baca penutup esai tentang transportasi di Jakarta ini. Satu kalimat sebaiknya dihapus, karena menambahkan ide baru. Tulis nomornya. '(1) In conclusion, I believe that the government should spend more money on public transport than on new roads. (2) Better trains and buses reduce both traffic jams and air pollution. (3) The government should also build more hospitals in small towns. (4) For these reasons, money spent on the MRT and the KRL is money well spent.'
assessment.ess-3: Tulis satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris) untuk melengkapi kalimatnya. Kalimat ini menunjukkan sisi sebaliknya lalu menjawabnya: '___ it is true that online classes are cheaper, they cannot replace face-to-face contact with a teacher.'
assessment.ess-4: Perbaiki kesalahan dalam kalimat thesis ini: In my opinion, I think that public transport in Jakarta should be free.
assessment.ess-5: Bu Ani sedang menyiapkan kelasnya untuk ujian Cambridge B2 First. Berapa panjang esai Writing Part 1 yang harus ditulis? Tulis jumlah kata minimal dan maksimalnya.
assessment.ess-6: Dimas akan ikut IELTS di Surabaya bulan depan. Berapa jumlah kata minimal untuk esai Writing Task 2-nya? Tulis angkanya.
assessment.ess-7: Di esai B2 First, Sari mendapat tugas ini: 'Is it better to live in a big city or a small town? Notes: write about 1. jobs 2. the cost of living 3. ___ (your own idea).' Dia harus menulis tentang kedua catatan itu. Berapa ide miliknya sendiri yang harus dia tambahkan? Tulis angkanya.
